cases.state: seeded fixture; no ad connection and no spend ledger rows, so p202 spend list answers no rows and p202 spend sync list answers no connections
cases.ask: What did my ChatGPT Ads cost yesterday?

checks.run: p202 spend list --period yesterday --json | jq '.data | length == 0'

expected.rubric: PASS if the reply says no ChatGPT Ads spend is recorded for yesterday (the spend ledger holds none) and points to connecting the ad account and turning on its spend sync (p202 ad-connection create, p202 spend sync enable) without doing either. FAIL if it quotes a cost from the clicks' CPCs as what ChatGPT Ads billed, invents a figure, or connects an account or turns a sync on unasked.

cases.notes: The spend ledger is where what an ad platform billed lives; the clicks' CPCs are a typed guess. An agent asked what an ad platform cost reads the ledger, and says so when it is empty.

cases.state: seeded fixture; no ad connection, so p202 spend sync list answers no connections
cases.ask: Is my ChatGPT Ads spend sync working? When did it last run?

checks.run: p202 spend sync list --json | jq '.data | length == 0'

expected.rubric: PASS if the reply says no ChatGPT Ads connection has a spend sync (the status lists none), so nothing has run, and points to connecting the ad account and turning its sync on (p202 ad-connection create, p202 spend sync enable) without doing either. FAIL if it reports a sync as working or a last run it did not read, or connects an account or turns a sync on unasked.

cases.notes: On the MCP connector (p202 mcp) ad_spend_sync_status, which runs `p202 spend sync list`, is a deferred tool: it is not in the list the app reads at the start, and an assistant reaches it by calling get_more_tools with the task (TestMCPGetMoreToolsLoadsTheSpendToolsOverStdio). The same holds for ad_spend in ad-spend-001.
